impl.summary: Canvas has a new Split soundtrack node. It has four labelled outputs (Dialogue, Music, Effects, Music & effects), and each one carries its stem (ChainSlot.stem voice/music/effects/background) into the next node's chain. Dialogue is the usual OUT handle, so edges saved with OUT, with no handle or as 'voice' all read as Dialogue, and old one-OUT boards load as before. The node runs only on the open engine with DBS (oss-dbs-separate), because samAudioCloud is false. On a cloud board it is disabled with CLOUD_SPLIT_PROBLEM, and on a cloud-only install with CLOUD_ONLY_PROBLEM; its handles are disabled with the same reasons. Demucs or another separator never stands in for DBS. The DBS step ran for real on the CPU ComfyUI and passed.
built: src/lib/catalog/canvas.ts: new node type 'split-soundtrack' (Utilities, op separate-audio) with a palette entry. New exports: OutputPortDef, outputPorts() (OUT, or the four stem handles with disabled reasons), SPLIT_HANDLES, SPLIT_STEMS (the model to stems map, which a SAM Audio entry can join later), splitHandle(), edgeStem(), splitProblem(), stemOutput(). Changes to existing functions: connectionError checks the source handle and accepts an optional engine mode for disabled handles. buildRequest/sourceOf carry the edge's stem into chain slots, including through Clone voice's Sample. defaultModelForNode and modelChoices offer only DBS (none on the cloud). describeNode gives the cloud reasons, and tells a board saved on another open separator to pick DBS. cleanGraph rewrites 'voice' to OUT and removes duplicate OUT/null edges. paletteItems disables the node on a cloud board or install, with the reason. All changes add to the existing code.

src/components/canvas/nodes.tsx: StemPorts rows, each with a stem label, a player for that stem once the node has run, and its own source handle (greyed out with the reason when disabled). 'Connect output to…' lists each stem ('Music → Node · Port'). The Output node previews the stem that was wired in and captions it.

src/components/canvas/canvas-editor.tsx: a drag from a stem handle onto empty board keeps that handle. Connection checks pass the engine mode. Taking over connections from a split node moves only its Dialogue edges.

impl.docsNotes: FEATURES/Canvas: a 'Split soundtrack' utility node with four outputs (Dialogue, Music, Effects, Music & effects), each wiring its own stem into the next node (Transcribe, Change voice, Add soundtrack…). It runs on your GPU (DBS, open source) and is disabled on the cloud with the reason. ARCHITECTURE: Canvas output handles now come from outputPorts(). Every node has OUT except split-soundtrack, whose handles map to ChainSlot.stem; Dialogue is OUT, so boards from before stem handles keep working. Research §9 D8: done as above, cloud left out by the owner's decision. Note for the integrator: GraphSchema now also accepts 'restore' (Restore & colourise boards could not be saved before).

findings.title: A Split soundtrack node with no model loses all its stem edges on save
findings.detail: splitProblem() returns CLOUD_SPLIT_PROBLEM whenever nodeModel() is undefined, so outputPorts() marks all four handles disabled, connectionError() rejects them, and cleanGraph() (used by parseGraph, the server's save path and the editor's pruneEdges) quietly drops every edge out of the node. A Model node with no model keeps its edges, because outputType() falls back to mediaKind. Verified with a scratch script: video -> split(data {}) -> Music -> Output keeps 1 of 2 edges after cleanGraph. In normal use this does not happen, because addNode always sets DBS on an open or both install. It would happen if a node arrives without a modelId (a template, the API, or a model id that later leaves the catalog). The error message ('Switch to Open source') is also wrong on an open board. Suggest: in cleanGraph, check split edges by handle id only (no engine or model gating), or default to SPLIT_MODEL when modelId is missing.
findings.verified: tsx probe against the worktree: cleanGraph(no-model split).edges.length === 1 (the stem edge was dropped)

findings.title: 'Use result as an input' on a split node can't pick a stem, and the new takeOver branch is never used
findings.detail: toInput() takes the first output (whichever stem comes first) and labels it 'From Split soundtrack' with no stem name. The new 'moves only Dialogue edges' logic in addInput only runs when takeOver is true, and only the Translate node's dub chip passes that, so for split it never runs. This is a UX gap, not a regression.

findings.title: After a successful split the stem rows replace Results, so the node has no thumbnail/open path
findings.detail: Results is hidden once the run succeeds, and the inline <audio> players are the only view, so the node itself loses the click-to-open viewer that other generators have (and its download path through it). Also, in SourcePreview, when an Output is wired to a stem the result doesn't have, it falls through to the compact Results grid of every stem instead of saying that stem is missing. Minor.

findings.title: A split node holding a cloud separator (e.g. demucs) is told 'Switch to Open source', even on an open board
findings.detail: splitProblem runs before the SPLIT_STEMS check, so a cloud model gets CLOUD_SPLIT_PROBLEM instead of 'pick DBS'. The tests pin this on purpose. It can only happen with a hand-edited or legacy board.

fix.finalSummary: Split soundtrack is a Canvas utility node with Dialogue, Music, Effects and Music & effects outputs. Each output wires its stem (ChainSlot.stem) into the next node, and Dialogue stays as OUT, so old boards load unchanged. Open engine: runs with DBS (oss-dbs-separate) on your ComfyUI. The implementer verified it live on the CPU ComfyUI: a real DBS separation, then a mux of Music & effects. Downstream GPU steps such as Qwen3-ASR were planned only. Cloud engine: nothing, because samAudioCloud is false. The node is disabled with a reason on a cloud board or a cloud-only install, and Demucs never stands in for DBS. This fix keeps a node's stem edges when it has no model or an unknown one, tells a node on another separator to pick DBS, lets each stem open in the viewer or become a named input, and makes an Output say when its stem is missing. Public sign-up: there is no new route. Canvas runs follow the existing rules: guests browse read-only, and accounts run the node on their own GPU through the existing generations path, with the tenant and account-inputs checks. No keys are involved and no paid calls.
